preserved_fields.title: Press Credential Elimination and Journalist Targeting - Government Media Access Destruction
preserved_fields.description_short: Press Credential Elimination and Journalist Targeting - Government Media Access Destruction
preserved_fields.subcategory: Press Freedom Elimination and Journalist Persecution
preserved_fields.description_long: Donald Trump systematically eliminated government press credentials and media access by revoking accreditation for journalists who reported critically on administration policies while implementing Project 2025's plan to 'use all tools at disposal to investigate leaks' and prosecute reporters' sources under the Espionage Act for routine newsgathering activities. The comprehensive press freedom destruction represented Trump's implementation of authoritarian media control that transformed government transparency from democratic principle into criminal offense, with journalists facing prosecution for reporting on government misconduct while losing access to official proceedings and information sources. The credential elimination included ending White House press briefings, restricting congressional access, eliminating agency briefings, and denying accreditation to independent journalists while providing exclusive access to conservative media outlets that promoted administration propaganda rather than factual reporting. Trump's media targeting violated First Amendment press freedom protections by using federal law enforcement to investigate journalists while treating routine news reporting as criminal activity subject to surveillance and prosecution under anti-terrorism and espionage statutes designed for foreign agents rather than domestic media. The press access destruction created what journalism advocates called return to authoritarian media control where government information became propaganda distribution rather than public accountability, with independent journalism facing systematic persecution through credential denial and source prosecution. The journalist targeting represented Project 2025's vision of media controlled by government loyalty rather than press freedom, transforming news reporting from public service into criminal activity while eliminating transparency mechanisms that had historically exposed government corruption and held officials accountable for violations of law and public trust.

organization_tags: North Dakota State University Agricultural Trade Monitor

preserved_fields.title: Agricultural Sector Devastated: China Soybean Exports Collapse 72%, $14.9B Loss
preserved_fields.description_short: Agricultural Sector Devastated: China Soybean Exports Collapse 72%, $14.9B Loss
preserved_fields.description_long: China's retaliatory tariffs in 2025 reduced U.S. agricultural exports to China from $24.5 billion in 2024 to just $8.4 billion in 2025, a two-thirds decline and the lowest annual figure in over two decades, per NDSU Agricultural Trade Monitor analysis. NDSU estimated the annualized China-specific agricultural export shortfall at $14.9 billion — 41% larger than the $10.6 billion shortfall during the 2018–2019 trade war. Soybeans accounted for $6.8 billion of the loss; beef and cotton each contributed $1.3 billion; corn $333 million; and tree nuts $964 million. For the first time in more than 20 years, Chinese importers purchased no soybeans from the U.S. autumn 2025 harvest, forcing American farmers to store their crops as prices fell to a five-year low. Brazil's soybean exports to China hit record levels in 2025, topping 85 million metric tons — an 18% increase — as U.S. market share evaporated.

preserved_fields.title: SEC Drops 60%+ of Crypto Enforcement Cases in Mass Regulatory Capitulation
preserved_fields.description_short: SEC Drops 60%+ of Crypto Enforcement Cases in Mass Regulatory Capitulation
preserved_fields.description_long: Within weeks of Trump's inauguration, the Securities and Exchange Commission under acting chair Mark Uyeda began systematically dropping enforcement actions against the crypto industry, which had spent more than $100 million supporting Trump's election. By February 21, 2025, the SEC dismissed its nearly two-year case against Coinbase, the largest U.S. crypto exchange, which had been charged with operating as an unregistered securities exchange. On March 20, 2025, the SEC dropped its four-year case against Ripple Labs and its XRP token. The agency also dropped or froze cases against Kraken, Gemini, Binance, and Robinhood. A December 2025 New York Times investigation found that the SEC had eased up on more than 60% of the crypto cases that were in progress at the start of Trump's second term — a retreat from a single industry with no legal precedent. The investigation into Justin Sun, who had invested $45 million in Trump's World Liberty Financial, was settled in March 2025 for $10 million with no admission of wrongdoing, after being paused following his WLF investment. Senator Elizabeth Warren demanded explanations for the apparent connection between Sun's investment in the Trump family business and the SEC's decision to drop its case against him. The mass regulatory pullback directly enriched the crypto industry that had funded Trump's election while benefiting the Trump family, which held billions in crypto assets subject to SEC oversight.

title: Federal Employee Mass Purge - Loyalty Test Government

prior_terminal_row.title: Federal Employee Mass Purge - Loyalty Test Government
prior_terminal_row.description_short: Federal Employee Mass Purge - Loyalty Test Government
prior_terminal_row.description_medium: During the first two months of his second term, Donald Trump dismissed thousands of federal employees, describing them as “Biden bureaucrats.” The firing campaign reached career civil servants across several departments, including Justice, State, Defense and Health and Human Services. Trump framed the removals as accountability. The dismissals raised questions about replacing career expertise with political loyalty across the executive branch.
prior_terminal_row.description_long: In his first two months of his second presidency, Donald Trump fired thousands of federal employees in what he called a purge of 'Biden bureaucrats,' though many were nonpartisan career civil servants who had served under multiple administrations. The mass firing represented the most extensive politicization of the federal government in American history, as Trump sought to install loyalists throughout the executive branch regardless of qualifications or experience. The purge targeted not just political appointees but career employees in agencies like Justice, State, Defense, and Health and Human Services, eliminating institutional knowledge and expertise built over decades. Trump justified the mass firings by claiming these employees had 'weaponized' the government against him, despite most being nonpartisan professionals who had served Republican and Democratic administrations alike. The systematic removal of experienced civil servants created chaos throughout the federal government, as critical functions were left unstaffed or run by inexperienced political appointees. The purge extended to scientists, economists, lawyers, and other professionals whose expertise was deemed threatening to Trump's political agenda. In his March 14, 2025 speech to the Justice Department, Trump explicitly described the firings as part of his campaign for 'accountability' against those who had opposed him. The mass purge represented the completion of Trump's authoritarian capture of the federal government, transforming professional civil service into a loyalty-based patronage system where expertise was subordinated to political fealty.
